messages:
liz: quick follow-up on the on-prem upgrade RFC — proposing a 'fast repair' / rollback-fastpath for airgapped installs when a partial apply (powercut, disk full, op error) leaves a node in a half-applied state. thoughts?
shreya: short answer: yes, we need it. long answer: prefer metadata-first + commit-marker pattern so we can repair without re-transferring huge blobs. avoids extra bandwidth and operator pain.
omar: agree on metadata-first, but we need to ensure cryptographic proof of 'what should be here' so repair doesn't accept a truncated or malicious blob sitting on disk. signed manifest + chunk hash ledger is minimum.
kevin: operator UX question — how would an operator trigger the fastpath vs full reapply? cli flag? automatic?
liz: propose both: auto-detect failed commit and attempt fastpath repair; fall back to full reapply if verification fails or missing chunks. manual CLI: `rdeploy repair --fastpath` with dry-run.
amy (product): what are the rollback semantics? can we guarantee idempotency? i.e., risk of double-apply if operator retries mid-repair.
shreya: design: apply order = metadata (manifests, symlinks) -> blob placement (chunks) -> commit-marker (signed) -> activate. commit-marker is single atomic swap (rename) so activation is clear. if repair sees missing commit-marker it replays to reach that marker. idempotent if operations are implemented as rename/compare-and-swap and blob writes are write-to-temp+rename.
omar: also include a monotonic 'apply-seq' in the commit-marker signed by control-plane key. repair verifies seq and chunk hashes. if seq mismatch, we reject fastpath.
kevin: sketch for CLI output and operator flow:
```
# dry-run
rdeploy repair --fastpath --dry-run
# attempt repair
rdeploy repair --fastpath --max-attempts=3 --progress
```
logs should show which chunks were missing and whether we pulled them from local seed cache or need full reapply.
shreya: local seed cache idea is important. device keeps a small ring buffer of recent blobs (configurable), so many transient failures repair without airgap transfer. retention default 72h?
liz: infra-bot reports: onprem-pack-v2.3.1 CI:✓ build, ✓ integration tests, blocked: size-smoke flake — irrelevant here.
omar: corner case: what if chunk present but corrupted on disk? we verify via hash ledger. if corruption, we either re-fetch from local seed or mark for full reapply. need policy for 'corruption threshold' (e.g., >5% of chunks => full reapply).
kevin: question: how do we sign the commit-marker in totally offline installs? we have control-plane signing during bundle creation, so marker includes that sig; node only verifies. no new external key required.
shreya: operational GC: we must keep old commit-markers + blobs for rollback window X. propose default rollback window 72h, configurable up to 30d. GC must not delete blobs referenced by any marker younger than retention.
amy (product): include operator-facing warnings: 'fastpath may not recover from missing seed; will fallback to full reapply. use when network constraints are strict.' docs need examples and recommended retention defaults.
liz: concrete marker example (proposal):
```
{
  "apply_seq": 12345,
  "manifest_sha256": "b3f4...",
  "chunk_hashes": ["a1...","b2...", "c3..."],
  "timestamp": 1680000000,
  "signature": "BASE64_SIG"
}
```
Repair algorithm (high level):
1) verify signed marker for target seq.
2) ensure manifests present and valid.
3) scan chunks; verify hashes. fetch missing/corrupt from local seed cache (if present).
4) if all verified, write commit-marker atomically and activate. else mark for full reapply.
shreya: also add an "apply-log" file recording attempted repairs with minimal metadata (seq, missing-chunks, operator-id) to aid postmortem and avoid thrashing.
omar: on the attestation side, add optional HSM-assisted key-unwrap step for airgapped key materials on-prem. not blocking for MVP but call it out.
kevin: testing plan: small PoC on 3 nodes with induced disk failures and SEQ jumps; measure mean time-to-repair for fastpath vs full reapply; goal: <10% of nodes fallthrough to full reapply.
liz: timeline: I'll open an RFC follow-up doc next week with diagrams, the marker schema, CLI UX, and PoC plan. asking: who can pair on PoC?
shreya: I can help with runtime/atomicity test harness.
omar: I'll take the verification + signing pieces.
amy (product): I'll draft the operator docs and add warnings + retention defaults.
kevin: I'll wire up CLI and unit tests.
liz: awesome — will post RFC link in this thread when created. quick note: add telemetry counters: repair_attempts, fastpath_success, fastpath_fail_reason to console metrics so we can observe in Dedicated/Hosted rollouts. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-checker: onprem-pack-v2.3.1 - size-smoke flake re-run queued.
shreya: one more perf note — verify chunk-hashes lazily in parallel to reduce latency; but commit only after all checks pass. avoid sequential IO.
omar: agreed. also consider bloom filter in manifest to speed 'likely present' checks for large bundles.
amy (product): agreed on rollout telemetry and operator messaging. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
